brief.angle: A text model generating a 300-word essay at 30 words per second takes ten seconds, during which a phone screen renders 600 full video frames.
brief.measure: Comparing word-by-word streaming speed to phone display refresh frames over the same duration.
brief.calc: 300 words / 30 words per sec = 10 seconds; 10 seconds * 60 frames per sec = 600 frames.
sources: Assumed text generation speed of 30 words per second
Standard mobile display refresh rate of 60 frames per second
brief.why_now: Direct comparison between local screen rendering speeds and text generation delays.

beats.say: Your screen draws six hundred frames for one short essay.
AI text streams thirty words every second.
A phone display refreshes sixty times per second.
The display timing runs double the speed of incoming words.
A three-hundred-word answer takes ten seconds to finish.
Over those ten seconds, the GPU renders six hundred frames.
Three hundred of those frames contained zero new text.
The GPU redrew identical pixels three hundred times waiting for tokens.
Half of the visual renders produced no screen change.
Your phone battery wastes half its rendering power repainting a static cursor during your homework.
